content.intro: Learn privacy and data retention through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Privacy and Data Retention matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines privacy and data retention as part of security and privacy. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Collecting only necessary data; Restricting access to personal information; Retention and deletion rules; Sensitive exports and backups; Logging without storing unnecessary private data; Django's security documentation covers these major attack classes and its current deployment; guidance should serve as the baseline for the course's security lessons.. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Collecting only necessary data
items.text: Collecting only necessary data affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Restricting access to personal information
items.text: Restricting access to personal information is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Retention and deletion rules
items.text: For Retention and deletion rules, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Sensitive exports and backups
items.text: Sensitive exports and backups should be planned for the actual hosting topology: configuration, permissions, resource limits, observability, rollback/recovery and a testable operating procedure all matter.

items.title: Logging without storing unnecessary private data
items.text: Logs should include enough structured context to debug events but omit credentials, tokens, payment data and sensitive user content. Define retention, access and alert rules.
